Subject: BYOK escrow + local KMS proxy — clarifications and acceptance criteria request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our infra team asked me to consolidate a short list of acceptance criteria for the BYOK / local KMS proxy flow so we can get security sign-off. Two areas they called out: (1) the escrow workflow and evidence for key custody (attestations, proof-of-possession), and (2) egress & telemetry — we need to prove minimal cross-border telemetry and be able to demonstrate token wrapping events for audits.

Can you confirm the following please:
- What artifacts will Redwood provide as evidence of the BYOK handoff and HSM attestation?
- How does the local KMS proxy minimize egress? We want a tight egress allowlist and a pattern for emergency fallbacks.
- Rotation expectations: recommended cadence and mechanisms for operator-initiated rotations (no downtime desirable).
- Audit log retention: what fields are captured and how long are immutable records retained?

We attached our security questionnaire (medidata-byo-questionnaire.xlsx) with some specifics. If you can send a short acceptance checklist and any diagrams (network/egress) that would be ideal — we need to prepare the package for our compliance review next Friday.

Appreciate it,
Sophie Liao

Subject: Re: BYOK escrow + local KMS proxy — clarifications and acceptance criteria request

Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short draft acceptance checklist and a network egress diagram for your review (redwood-byo-proxy-draft-v1.pdf; network-egress-diagram.png). High-level answers below; Ben and Laura from our security/ops team are looped to fill in runbook detail.

Quick answers:
- Artifacts / evidence:
  * HSM attestation report (measurement + vendor cert) signed at ceremony time
  * PKCS#7-style key-wrapping receipt showing key ID, wrapping key thumbprint, and time stamps
  * Operator action logs (who performed export/wrapping) with immutable audit events (sha256 hashes archived)
- Egress minimization:
  * KMS proxy runs inside your VPC with one outbound allowlist entry: to the Redwood control-plane collector for heartbeat/alerts (TLS 443 to specific IPs).
  * All key-wrapping operations are local; only signed wrapping receipts (no raw key material) leave the VPC.
  * Emergency fallback: a pre-authorized short-lived cross-region tunnel that requires multi-admin approval via our console and DocuSign-signed request (we log approval).
- Rotation & downtime:
  * Recommended: split-custody rotation every 90 days for KEKs; more frequent ephemeral wrapping tokens (daily) for session keys.
  * Our runtime supports dual-write rolling rotation with prefix caching so service threads don’t stall — typically zero-downtime for reads, minor write windows for rewrapping (<60s).
- Audit logs:
  * Capture: event_type, actor_id, key_id, operation, wrapping_key_thumbprint, timestamp, request_id, SHA256(wrapping_receipt).
  * Immutable retention: 7 years archived; short-term hot logs 90 days. Archive signed with time-stamp authority.

Open questions for Medidata team:
- Do you require HSM vendor on-prem installation or is a FedRAMP-equivalent hosted HSM acceptable?
- Any regulatory constraints on cross-border telemetry beyond standard US/EU rules?

We can tighten the checklist once Ben/Laura add operator runbook items. Proposed next step: 30-min call today at 4pm ET to walk the checklist and sign off on required artifacts.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: BYOK escrow + local KMS proxy — acceptance criteria and egress telemetry

Looping in a few operational specifics Sophie asked for. I'll keep this tight to items you can slot directly into the acceptance checklist.

Network / deployment:
- Proxy placement: single AZ private subnet with NAT gateway disabled for general instances. KMS proxy uses a route to a managed egress bastion (we provide IPs) — all other outbound is blocked at the VPC level.
- Ports & endpoints: only outbound TCP/443 to our collector IP ranges; inbound from your application subnets over mTLS (client certs for service identities).

Escrow & attestation:
- At handoff we provide an HSM attestation bundle (TPM-style quote) + a signed wrapping receipt. The wrapping receipt includes a PKCS#1 signature from the HSM’s signing key and is verifiable offline.
- Escrow storage options: (a) customer-managed escrow (preferred) in your S3/Azure Blob with object-level encryption; (b) Redwood-managed encrypted escrow with customer KMS envelope-wrapped key where we never hold plaintext. Choose (a) if you need full custody proof.

Rotation & operator actions:
- Operator separation: rotation requires two distinct operator approvals (operator + security approver). We provide a CLI that emits signed operator-proofs which become part of the immutable audit event.
- Emergency unwrapping: policy-driven with automatic revoke if thresholds exceeded; ephemeral session tokens scoped to single rewrap operation.

Telemetry & logs:
- Telemetry minimal: heartbeat + summary metrics (success/fail counts, latency) — no key identifiers or plaintext.
- Audit export: signed weekly bundles to your configured archive location; single-click verification tool provided.

I'll add these as bullets to the draft PDF and push a v1.1 after the call. If Medidata prefers, we can prep a short demo of an operator rotation (90s walkthrough).

Ben Carter
Product Security — Redwood Inference
